details.body: BiologySnapshot struct in crates/tank_api/src/handlers/snapshot.rs (line 144-162) is missing the sub_adult_count field. TankSnapshot now has sub_adult_count (snapshot.rs:39) and it's populated from state.animal.sub_adult.count (snapshot.rs:138), but the /biology API endpoint silently omits sub-adults. Add `pub sub_adult_count: u32` to BiologySnapshot and populate it from `s.sub_adult_count` in get_biology().

The conductivity calculation in crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:174 uses a bare magic number 0.65 (`self.tds_mg_per_l(volume_l) / 0.65`). Per the project prompt's requirement that 'conversion factors should be defined as named constants, not magic numbers scattered through rendering code', this should be a named constant (e.g., `const TDS_TO_CONDUCTIVITY_FACTOR: f64 = 0.65;`) with a doc comment explaining its derivation and limitations.

The chemistry_field_semantics metadata (snapshot.rs:100-112) only documents the new-style field names. It should also document `do_mg_l` and `do_sat_mg_l` (which appear in the chemistry response at lines 57-58) since these lack the explicit unit suffix pattern used by other fields and could be confused with dissolved organic matter.

The GH/KH conversion constants in water.rs (lines 5-6, and the inline coefficients 2.497 and 4.118 at line 162) are bare magic numbers without documentation of their chemical derivation. Like the N/P conversion factors in conversions.rs, these should be named constants with doc comments explaining the molar mass ratios they represent (Ca²+ equivalent weight → CaCO3, Mg²+ equivalent weight → CaCO3).

`snapshot_response_json()` only backfills legacy aliases for TAN/NH3/NO2/NO3/PO4/TDS/conductivity in `crates/tank_api/src/handlers/snapshot.rs:86-96`, but `TankSnapshot` also renamed `dissolved_inorganic_carbon_mg_l` to `dissolved_inorganic_carbon_mg_c_per_l` in `crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:20-21`. As a result, `/snapshot`, `/time/step`, `/load`, and scenario-load responses no longer contain the old DIC key, so pre-rename API clients that deserialize the old snapshot shape will fail even though the other renamed fields were kept backward-compatible. Add the missing top-level `dissolved_inorganic_carbon_mg_l` alias and include it in `legacy_chemistry_aliases`.

`OMITTED_TDS_CONTRIBUTORS` in `crates/tank_api/src/handlers/snapshot.rs:9-12` says the 7-ion estimate omits "untracked nitrogen and phosphorus ions". That is false for this model: TAN/NH3, nitrite, nitrate, and phosphate are tracked and surfaced in the same response; they are merely excluded from the TDS/conductivity proxy. Reword this metadata to say those tracked species are omitted from the estimate, otherwise the new self-description still misstates model scope and can mislead users about what the simulation actually tracks.

`crates/tank_tui/src/screens/chemistry.rs:51-59` and `crates/tank_tui/src/screens/overview.rs:49-58` stop at `Est. TDS (7-ion)` / `Est. conductivity`, but never tell the TUI user which seven ions are counted or that nitrate/phosphate/organics are excluded. The API now carries that scope metadata, so the UI portion of this bead is still incomplete: a TUI user cannot actually tell what the estimate includes or omits, which was part of the acceptance criteria for the chemistry-semantics change.

Add deserialization aliases for the renamed snapshot chemistry fields. `TankSnapshot` now only declares the new names such as `tan_mg_n_per_l`, `nitrite_mg_n_per_l`, `nitrate_mg_n_per_l`, `phosphate_mg_p_per_l`, and `estimated_conductivity_us_cm` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:9-28`), but the TUI still parses `/snapshot`, `/time/step`, and `/load` responses straight into `TankSnapshot` (`crates/tank_tui/src/api_client.rs:28-46`, `crates/tank_tui/src/api_client.rs:70-79`). That means a newer client can no longer talk to an older API server that still emits only `tan_mg_l`/`nitrite_mg_l`/etc. even though this bead explicitly called out backward compatibility for API consumers. Add `#[serde(alias = ...)]` coverage or an equivalent compatibility DTO so version-skewed clients do not fail to deserialize snapshots.

Make the overview screen label the conductivity/TDS values as estimates, not definitive readings. The main summary line still renders `7-ion TDS ... Cond ...` in `crates/tank_tui/src/screens/overview.rs:53-55`, even though the underlying fields are `estimated_tds_7_ion_mg_per_l` and `estimated_conductivity_us_cm`. The chemistry screen was updated correctly, but the overview screen is still user-facing output that can read like true TDS/conductivity rather than a 7-ion proxy. Rename that line to something like `Est. TDS (7-ion)` and `Est. conductivity` there as well.

Add a test asserting that REFERENCE_SA_V_CM2_PER_L matches the actual default TankState geometry. Currently the constant 1000.0/19.0 is documented to match the default 40x25 cm footprint with 3 cm substrate (~19 L net), but nothing enforces this at compile-time or test-time. If the default substrate depth, geometry dimensions, or displacement model change, compute_o2_kla silently produces incorrect normalization (ratio != 1.0) for the default tank. A single test like `assert!((state.geometry.surface_area_cm2() / state.water_volume_l() - REFERENCE_SA_V_CM2_PER_L).abs() < 0.01)` on a default TankState would catch this.

The TUI api_client normalize_snapshot_object function adds canonical fields from legacy aliases but does not strip the legacy or API-injected metadata fields (chemistry_field_semantics, estimated_tds_scope, legacy_chemistry_aliases) before calling serde_json::from_value. This works only because TankSnapshot omits #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]. Add a test to api_client that deserializes a full snapshot_response_json() output (which includes all metadata fields) through parse_snapshot_value, verifying the TUI client can handle the enriched API response end-to-end — not just hand-crafted legacy-only payloads.

Fix the snapshot TDS/conductivity projection so it is derived from the same fresh carbonate solve as the snapshot pH/CO2 values. In `crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:78-90`, `TankSnapshot::from_state()` recomputes `carbonate_eq` from authoritative DIC + alkalinity, but `estimated_tds_7_ion_mg_per_l` / `estimated_conductivity_us_cm` still come from `chemistry.tds_mg_per_l()` and `chemistry.conductivity_us_cm()`. Those helpers read `WaterState::bicarbonate_mg_total` through `crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:189-240`, and that field is only a cache. If DIC/alkalinity changed without a preceding `resolve_carbonate_state()`, the snapshot can report internally inconsistent chemistry: fresh pH/CO2 with stale bicarbonate-backed TDS. Derive the bicarbonate contribution from `carbonate_eq.hco3_mmol_per_l` inside `TankSnapshot::from_state()` (or force a carbonate refresh before reading TDS), and add a regression test that mutates DIC/alkalinity while leaving the cache stale.

Centralize the 7-ion scope metadata next to the actual TDS calculation instead of maintaining separate hardcoded copies in core, API, and TUI. The authoritative ion set is implicit in `crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:235-242`, but the explanatory strings are duplicated in `crates/tank_api/src/handlers/snapshot.rs:8-12` / `crates/tank_api/src/handlers/snapshot.rs:121-125` and again in `crates/tank_tui/src/screens/mod.rs:11-15`. Move the tracked/omitted-ion metadata into `tank_core` and have both API and TUI consume that shared definition.

In overview.rs, the NH3 label reads `NH3-N {:.4} mg N/L` while in chemistry.rs it reads `Free NH3-N {:.5} mg NH3-N/L`. The unit suffixes differ: overview says 'mg N/L' (element basis) while chemistry says 'mg NH3-N/L' (which is the same thing but uses a different notation). Both are technically correct for the same quantity, but the inconsistency may confuse users comparing the two screens. Standardize on one label — either 'mg N/L' or 'mg NH3-N/L' — across both screens.

`crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:11-23,26-45` introduces legacy field mappings but does not apply them during `TankSnapshot` deserialization. Compatibility for renamed chemistry keys currently lives only in `crates/tank_tui/src/api_client.rs:119-145`, so any other Rust consumer that deserializes legacy `/snapshot` or `/load` payloads directly into `tank_core::TankSnapshot` will still fail with missing `*_mg_n_per_l` / `*_mg_p_per_l` fields. Move the compatibility into `tank_core` itself (for example with `#[serde(alias = ...)]` or a shared normalizer) instead of making each client reimplement the shim.

`crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:87-111` now computes TDS/conductivity from a fresh carbonate solve, but the public state helpers still read the cached `water.bicarbonate_mg_total` via `crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:207-240` and `crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:317-322`. The new test at `crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:256-289` explicitly asserts that snapshot values can exceed the cached helper values. That leaves two public APIs able to report different TDS/conductivity for the same `TankState`, which is a correctness/maintenance trap for any internal caller that does not go through `TankSnapshot`. Factor the fresh carbonate projection into a single shared helper or refresh the cache before every public accessor.
